<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard AUR package metadata and variable definitions at the global scope. No command substitutions (`$(...)` or backticks) are present that would execute code during sourcing. The `source` and `source_x86_64` arrays define URLs pointing to the package's own declared upstream (flawme/varn on GitHub), which is expected behavior. The `package()` function is defined but not executed at the top level; it would only run during the package phase, which `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not invoke. All variable expansions are standard shell parameter expansions without side effects. There is no obfuscation, no unexpected network destinations, and no exfiltration logic.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This `.SRCINFO` file describes a straightforward prebuilt binary AUR package (`varn-bin`) that downloads a single release binary and accompanying documentation from the project's own GitHub repository (`https://github.com/flawme/varn`).

All sources are fetched from the package's declared upstream (the `flawme/varn` GitHub organization), which is expected for a binary package. The binary itself is downloaded from the official GitHub releases endpoint (`/releases/download/v0.3.1/varn-linux-x86_64`), and all six documentation/license sources come from `raw.githubusercontent.com/flawme/varn` at a pinned tag (`v0.3.1`).

Every source — including the binary — has a concrete SHA256 checksum (no `SKIP` entries), which is good supply-chain hygiene. There are no suspicious URLs, no obfuscated content, no unexpected scripts, and no operations outside ordinary packaging practice. The package depends only on `glibc` and `libgcc`, which is appropriate for a static/native Linux binary.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard binary package with pinned upstream sources and proper checksums.</summary>
</security_assessment>

The configuration simply specifies that nvchecker should track the GitHub repository "flawme/varn" and monitor its releases (using "v" as a version prefix). There are no suspicious network destinations, no obfuscated code, no file operations, and no attempts to download or execute external code. This is a routine packaging maintenance tool configuration, consistent with standard AUR workflow practices.
</details>

This PKGBUILD is a standard AUR binary package for the `varn` project hosted at `https://github.com/flawme/varn`. All source files (documentation and license files) are fetched from the project's own GitHub raw content URL, and the prebuilt binary is downloaded from the project's own GitHub releases page. All sha256 checksums are properly provided for every source entry, including the binary — not SKIP'd.

The `package()` function performs only routine installation steps: placing the binary in `/usr/bin/`, documentation in `/usr/share/doc/`, and license files in `/usr/share/licenses/`. There are no suspicious operations such as `curl|sh`, `eval`, `base64` decoding, network exfiltration, modifications to system files outside the package scope, or any other indicators of supply-chain compromise. The dependencies (`glibc`, `libgcc`) are minimal and appropriate for a prebuilt Go/Rust-style static-ish binary.
</details>
